subject: CPRA addendum question — telemetry routing & service-provider vs resale classification
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Cho <natalie.cho@northhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: CPRA addendum question — telemetry routing & service-provider vs resale classification

Hi Natalie —

Thanks again for the continued momentum on the privacy addendum. We reviewed the draft you shared and had a quick legal/engineering question about telemetry flows that affects how we should sign the CPRA/US-state addendum language. Attaching a small flow diagram and our proposed clause edits (see attachments).

Short version: some telemetry (aggregate metrics, health pings, routing metadata) can transit a third-party CDN/cache layer operated by our infra partner. The data is ephemeral and used purely to deliver model outputs and improve runtime reliability. We want to ensure this behavior is captured under a "service provider / processor" model (i.e., no-sale, limited use) in the NorthHealth addendum rather than being treated as "resale" or "sale" under CPRA.

Two quick asks:
- Can you confirm NorthHealth's expectation for telemetry that passes through a third-party cache (no persistent identifiers stored, TTL <24h, encrypted in transit and at rest)?
- Would NorthHealth require explicit subprocessor-level commitments (onshore fallback, audit rights) before allowing the route, or would a general service-provider clause with described controls be sufficient?

We proposed some plaintext edits in redwood-psp-language-draft.docx to clarify limited use and permitted routing to subcontractors for delivery/availability reasons. If it helps, we can escalate a short three-way call with LegalOps to walk through the exact wording.

Thanks — short/clear answer preferred so we can get the addendum signed this week.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Staff Product Counsel, Redwood Inference
+1 415 555 0123

---
From: Natalie Cho <natalie.cho@northhealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@northhealth.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: CPRA addendum question — telemetry routing & service-provider vs resale classification

Hi Lukas —

Thanks for the clear note and the diagram — that helps. Short answers up front:
- If telemetry contains no persistent identifiers and is used only for delivery/availability/aggregation, NorthHealth views that as consistent with a service provider (processor) relationship; we are not expecting it to be treated as a sale.
- However, because NorthHealth is in the health vertical, we typically require (1) documented subprocessor commitments (data handling, encryption, deletion TTL) and (2) the ability to request evidence (SOC2 summary or equivalent) for any third party that receives telemetry beyond transient caching.

Two clarifications from our side:
1) If the cache can persist logs longer than 24 hours or material identifiers are present, we will treat that as potential sale-risk and need stronger contractual limits.
2) Onshore fallback: if the cache/spike routing sends traffic offshore for >12 hours during an outage, we will require an onshore fallback plan in the addendum.

I can have LegalOps provide a short template for the subprocessor commitments that we expect — would you prefer they send that directly to Priyom or route via you?

Regards,
Natalie Cho
Director, Security & Privacy, NorthHealth

---
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Natalie Cho <natalie.cho@northhealth.com>, LegalOps <legalops@northhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 12:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CPRA addendum question — telemetry routing & service-provider vs resale classification

Thanks Natalie — helpful. A couple of internal notes and a proposed insertion we should consider adding to the addendum (I pasted a short clause below).

Engineering notes:
- Current CDN partner (Edgelia) keeps transient metrics with TTL=12h by default; persistent logs are sent to our observability pipeline only with identifiers stripped and sampled at <=0.1%. We also support an onshore-only routing flag per-account.
- For NorthHealth, we can enable onshore-only routing and a reduced sampling profile at provisioning time. This is operational, not just legal.

Proposed clause (drafted for discussion):
"Service Provider Routing & Subprocessor Use. Redwood may engage third-party caching and delivery subprocessors to perform transient telemetry routing and availability functions. Such subprocessors will act only on Redwood's instructions and shall process telemetry solely for the purpose of delivering service and maintaining availability. Redwood shall ensure: (i) no persistent identifiers are stored by such subprocessors beyond 24 hours; (ii) telemetry stored or transmitted is encrypted in transit and at rest; (iii) customer-specific onshore fallback can be enabled upon request; and (iv) Redwood will provide reasonable evidence of third-party controls upon NorthHealth's written request (e.g., SOC 2 summary)."

Suggest we include the clause in the addendum and then have LegalOps confirm the template. Priyom — can you attach a short note on the specific observability sampling and log retention settings we can offer? I added that to redwood-psp-language-draft.docx.

-P

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Natalie Cho <natalie.cho@northhealth.com>, LegalOps <legalops@northhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CPRA addendum question — telemetry routing & service-provider vs resale classification

Lukas / Priyom / Natalie — quick follow-up from the contracts side.

Two items we should land on in the addendum text:
- Audit & evidence: specify acceptable evidence forms (SOC2 summary, ISAE-3000 attestation, or a vendor security questionnaire response) and a reasonable notice window (30 days).
- Deletion SLA: commit to deletion of any telemetry derived identifiers or customer-specific aggregates upon NorthHealth request within X days (suggest 30 days), with an exception window for legitimate operational retention (e.g., incident investigation capped at 60 days).

I will draft redlines with exact clause language if we can agree on the deletion window and evidence forms. Natalie — is 30 days/60 days reasonable for NorthHealth?

Thanks,
Laura
Sr. Contract Manager, Redwood Inference

---
From: Natalie Cho <natalie.cho@northhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@northhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 11:27:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: CPRA addendum question — telemetry routing & service-provider vs resale classification

Laura — 30/60 seems reasonable to us. For evidence, a SOC2 Type II summary within the last 12 months or an audited equivalent is preferred; an up-to-date vendor questionnaire response is acceptable as interim evidence. Notice window of 30 days for evidence is fine.

LegalOps will prepare the subprocessor commitment template and send it to Priyom; please expect a short form that we can incorporate into the addendum.

Thanks — looking forward to the signed addendum.

-Natalie

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CPRA addendum question — telemetry routing & service-provider vs resale classification

Great — thanks everyone for the quick turnaround and the alignment. Next steps: 
- Priyom: confirm operational settings (onshore-only flag + sampling) and paste into the addendum (I'll take Laura's redline and insert the agreed deletion/SOC language).
- LegalOps / Natalie: send the subprocessor commitment template to Priyom (LegalOps link expected by EOD Thu).
- Lukas/Laura: compile the final addendum with agreed clause and DocuSign envelope (I will include the NorthHealth-Privacy-Annex-v1.pdf and the telemetry-flow-diagram for context).

If all goes well we'll aim to have signatures by Friday. I put a DocuSign envelope in related links for tracking; please confirm receipt and any required changes.

Closing note: we will explicitly mark telemetry routed via third-party caches as "limited use — delivery and availability only" in the CPRA addendum to avoid classification as sale.

Best,
Lukas
Staff Product Counsel, Redwood Inference
